change.title: pr-37038-flat
change.description: Add Groups resource type and scopes to authorization schema
change.author: Cristian Sotomayor

findings.title: canManage() grants manage to admins that only have the VIEW scope
findings.body: `canManage()` calls `hasPermission(null, VIEW, MANAGE)`, so an admin with only an all-groups `view` permission passes. `GroupsResource` line 181 uses `auth.groups().requireManage()` to guard creating top-level groups, so a view-only admin can create them. The sibling `ClientPermissionsV2.canManage()` (line 73) checks `MANAGE` only, and so does the per-group `canManage(GroupModel)` at line 79. Use `hasPermission(null, AdminPermissionsSchema.MANAGE)`. The new Javadoc on `GroupPermissionEvaluator.canManage()` (lines 75-76) documents the same mistake and should be corrected too. `testViewGroups` does not catch this because it never tries a write with a view-only permission.

findings.title: getGroupIdsWithViewPermission iterates the wrong resources and returns resource UUIDs instead of group IDs
findings.body:
Per-group resources are created in `AdminPermissionsSchema.getOrCreateResource` (lines 118-127) with the group id as `name` and no `setType`. Only the all-groups resource (named "Groups") gets type `Groups`, in `init` at line 274. So `findByType(server, GROUPS_RESOURCE_TYPE, ...)` appears to return only the all-groups type resource. On top of that, the lambda passes `groupResource.getId()`, which is the resource UUID, to `hasPermission`. That method looks it up with `findByName(server, groupId)`, where the name is the group id, so it falls back to the all-groups resource. Finally it adds `groupResource.getId()` (a resource UUID, not a group id) to the result. Consequences:
- An admin with only per-group `view-members` gets an empty set. `searchForUser` then sets no `UserModel.GROUPS` restriction, so the DB query is unrestricted and relies on the post-filter. Counts from `getUsersCount(..., groupIds)` are wrong, and paging is applied before the filter.
- An admin with all-groups `view-members` gets a set containing a non-group UUID. That set is applied as the group restriction in `JpaUserProvider` (around line 762), so the search returns no users.

The tests pass only because the post-filter `canView(user)` goes through `canViewMembers`. Iterate resources by name, or iterate the realm's groups, use the group id for both the lookup and the result, and add a test for the user count and for all-groups `view-members`.

findings.title: Realms that already enabled admin permissions have no Groups type resource or new scopes
findings.body: `AdminPermissionsSchema.init` returns early when the permissions client already exists (line 250). A realm that enabled V2 before this change therefore has no `Groups` resource and none of the `manage-membership`, `manage-members` or `view-members` scopes. In that case `getResourceTypeResource` returns null, and `policyStore.findByResource(server, null)` here (and `resource.getScopes()` at line 152) would likely throw. `canViewByGroup`, `canView(group)` and similar calls would then fail for every non-role admin in that realm. `getOrCreateResource` would also throw "No scopes found." Is there a migration or lazy init for existing V2 realms, or is that accepted because the feature is experimental?

findings.title: Group removal listener now hits a V2 groups() that throws UnsupportedOperationException when both FGAP flags are on
findings.body: The listener is registered when `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ` (V1) is enabled, but `management()` returns `MgmtPermissionsV2` whenever `ADMIN_FINE_GRAINED_AUTHZ_V2` is enabled. The V2 flag does not depend on V1 (Profile.java line 58). With both flags on, deleting a group now reaches `GroupPermissionsV2.setPermissionsEnabled`, which throws. Before this change `groups()` was always the V1 class, so the delete worked. Client removal already has the same problem via `ClientPermissionsV2`. The tests enable only V2, so they do not exercise this. Make the listener skip V2, or have the V2 methods do nothing when called from it.

findings.title: Javadoc inaccuracies
findings.body: `requireManageMembers` (line 133) says it throws when `canManageMembership` is false; it should reference `canManageMembers`. `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` (line 145) says it returns a "Stream" but returns `Set<String>`. The `canManage()` doc (lines 75-76) says VIEW grants manage, which is the bug reported on `GroupPermissionsV2.java` line 70.

findings.title: Missing negative and count coverage
findings.body: `testViewGroups` never checks that a view-only admin cannot create or modify groups, which would have caught the `canManage()` bug. No test covers an all-groups `view-members` or `manage-members` permission, or `users().count()` for an admin with group-scoped permissions. Those are the paths that use `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission`. Line 68 also has a stray `;;`.

contracts.action: User search/count restricts results to groups the admin can view members of
contracts.equivalent_path: The old searchForUser guarded the call with `if (!auth.users().canView())` and then applied a `usersEvaluator::canView` filter. The same filter still runs in toRepresentation (UsersResource.java:460).
contracts.before_after: Now `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission()` is always called. It returns an empty set when `root.users().canView()` is true (GroupPermissionsV2.java:107, GroupPermissions.java:299), so the old guard is preserved. The removed filter is a duplicate of the one in toRepresentation, and the same change is made in BruteForceUsersResource.
contracts.visible_effect: Users list and count for admins with group-scoped permissions. The V2 set is wrong, as in the finding on GroupPermissionsV2.java line 121.
contracts.failure_mode: Wrong counts, or an empty list for all-groups view-members admins.

contracts.action: GroupPermissionsV2 evaluates group permissions against Groups type resources
contracts.before_after: It mirrors the users version: look up the specific resource by name, otherwise fall back to the type resource if it has policies. Unlike the users version it does not check that `permission.getResourceId()` equals the resource id. That check looks defensive only.
contracts.visible_effect: Group list, view, manage and membership operations for V2 admins.
contracts.failure_mode: The type resource is null for realms initialized before this change (AdminPermissionsSchema.init returns early at line 250). That would give an NPE or a 500, as the question on GroupPermissionsV2.java line 147 says.
contracts.open_question: Is there migration or lazy initialization for realms that already have the admin-permissions client?

summary:
Review of the V2 Groups resource type for fine-grained admin permissions. One blocker: `GroupPermissionsV2.canManage()` accepts the VIEW scope, so a view-only admin can create top-level groups. One fix: `getGroupIdsWithViewPermission` in V2 iterates the wrong resources and returns resource UUIDs rather than group ids, which makes user counts wrong and can empty the user search for all-groups view-members admins. The tests pass only because of the post-filter on each user. Three smaller points:
- Existing V2 realms won't have the new `Groups` resource or scopes.
- Deleting a group fails when both FGAP feature flags are on.
- A few Javadoc and test-coverage gaps.

The rest looks sound: the V1 refactor is behaviour-equivalent except that V1 `canViewMembers` now also accepts `manage-members`, and the removed duplicate filters are still applied in `toRepresentation`.
